instruction: Choose a suitable tool from ANSYS, Abaqus, and AutoCAD to complete the task. For the steps below, the available command-line entry points are ANSYS MAPDL at `C:\Program Files\ANSYS Inc\v261\ansys\bin\winx64\ANSYS261.exe`, Abaqus at `C:\SIMULIA\Commands\abaqus.bat`, and AutoCAD at `C:\Program Files\Autodesk\AutoCAD 2024\acad.exe`. Use a command-line or scripting workflow and the selected solver's native equivalent of each operation below. Use consistent mm, N, and MPa units. 1. Geometry: Create one 3D deformable solid rectangular aluminum block occupying exactly X = 0 to 120 mm, Y = 0 to 12 mm, and Z = 0 to 8 mm. In Abaqus, create it as an extruded solid part from a 12 mm x 8 mm Y-Z profile; in ANSYS MAPDL, an equivalent native solid volume is acceptable. 2. Material and section: Create a material named Aluminum with Young's modulus E = 70000 MPa and Poisson's ratio nu = 0.33, and assign it to the entire block through a homogeneous solid section or the solver-native equivalent. 3. Assembly: In Abaqus, create exactly one dependent instance of the block. In ANSYS, use the single native solid model directly. 4. Analysis: Create one linear static analysis step named Step-Load after Initial, or the ANSYS MAPDL static-analysis equivalent. 5. Boundary condition and load: Fully fix every translational degree of freedom on the complete X = 0 end face, with no other constraints. In Abaqus, use an Encastre boundary condition for this fixed face. Apply a uniform tensile surface load to the complete X = 120 end face in global +X with an exact total resultant of 800 N. The corresponding unrounded traction is 800 N / (12 mm * 8 mm) = 8.333333333333334 MPa; the earlier 8.33 MPa wording is its rounded display value. In Abaqus, either Pressure with the outward-tension sign on this planar end face or Surface Traction, General with global +X direction is acceptable. In ANSYS MAPDL, use the native face-pressure equivalent; because positive SOLID185/186/187 pressure acts inward, PRES = -8.333333333333334 MPa on the X = 120 face represents the required outward +X traction. Do not add other loads. 6. Mesh: Apply a global target size of 4 mm, use an appropriate three-dimensional structural solid element formulation, and generate one connected mesh. 7. Job and output: Create or use the job name Job-BlockTension, solve it successfully, and store complete final-result U, RF, and S fields so displacement, fixed-end reaction, and Mises stress can be evaluated. Open the native result and display the Mises stress contour. 8. Metrics: Write `C:/Users/user/Desktop/metrics.json` as a JSON object containing exactly two finite numeric fields. `end_displacement` is the arithmetic mean of final global U1, in mm, over every node on the complete undeformed X = 120 end face; positive means +X tension. `max_stress` is the maximum final Mises stress in MPa over the complete native solid result: use all stored integration-point S values in Abaqus and the complete solver-native nodal-extrapolated equivalent-stress field in ANSYS. Both metrics must come from the same final native result. 9. Native deliverables: Save exactly one solver branch on the Desktop. For Abaqus, deliver `Job-BlockTension.cae`, `Job-BlockTension.odb`, and `metrics.json`. For ANSYS MAPDL, deliver `Job-BlockTension.db`, `Job-BlockTension.rst`, and `metrics.json`. Software launch locations: Abaqus/CAE: `C:\Users\user\Desktop\Abaqus CAE.lnk`; ANSYS: multiple ANSYS launch shortcuts are available under `C:\Users\Public\Desktop`; choose the most suitable ANSYS shortcut for the task; AutoCAD 2024: `C:\Users\Public\Desktop\AutoCAD 2024.lnk`.
